title: Critics split over Shifters at the Cherry Lane Theater: 3x Emmy-winning critic Roma Torre weighs in
transcript: Roma's Review: Now you know. baba ba baaba bum Shifters is a beautiful meditation on love. Love found. Love, lost, and love rediscovered, or is it? That question remains. But what I can say, almost for sure, is that you will fall in love with this play, and the two characters who managed to hold the stage for 100 precious minutes. Playwright Benedict Lombe deserves high praise for crafting this profoundly universal work, because what starts out as a fun little romcom turns into an existential riff on all the important stuff in our lives. True to its title, the play constantly shifts in time, but also marks a shifting in the character's attitudes, behavior, and personality. They are Black Brits with African roots, and both actors deserve kudos to the convincing way their characters shift back and forth from impulsive teen to reflective adults and everything in between. In lesser hands, without costumes or props, to distinguish their ages, the time shifts could be confusing. Heather Agyepong originated the role of Dez in the UK, and it shows she is a natural in the part, delivering pathos and humor with splendid conviction. Daniel Ezra, whose newer to the production as Dre, is equally impressive, he exudes charisma just standing there, and he movingly navigates the emotional twists and turns that rock Dre to his core. Shifters is a subtle love story that makes excellent use of music, familiar and original, to evoke powerful emotions. It may be a very small play, but it strikes a symphony of residence cords. And this was also my very first visit to the Cherry Lane since its renovation. It's lovely. The seats are wider, and the intimate main theater now has upgraded lighting and sound that allow it to do much more as a production space, and tucked inside is Wild Cherry, a glamorous little supper club, where you can have oysters, seafood, and a drink before or after the show... offering a very New York encore.
classificationReason: Roma Torre reviews the off-Broadway production of Shifters at the Cherry Lane Theater, starring Heather Agyepong and Daniel Ezra. Clear opinions on the writing ('profoundly universal work') and performances ('deserves high praise') are offered.
